title: MIT Researchers Propose 'Economic Q' Framework for Fusion Power Plant Viability
detail: MIT professors Dennis Whyte (Nuclear Science & Engineering; CFS co-founder) and Andrew W. Lo (Sloan School of Management) published a framework in the Journal of Fusion Energy on August 10, 2026 proposing ten quantitative parameters — spanning scientific inputs, engineering durability, and capital costs — for assessing when a fusion power plant becomes commercially viable, anchored by a metric the authors call 'Economic Q': the ratio of capital generated to capital expended over a plant's operating lifetime. Whyte said the framework is 'completely agnostic to whatever fusion concept you use' because it scales to any reactor design or output level, aiming to give investors, policymakers, and developers a common yardstick independent of any single company's technology.

title: Fuse Energy's FAETON-X Sets Highest Publicly Documented Neutron Yield by a Fusion Company
detail: Fuse Energy Technologies reported on August 10, 2026 that its megajoule-class dense plasma focus device FAETON-X — operating at 65 kV and storing roughly 1 MJ of energy — produced a peak yield of (1.27±0.27)×10^12 deuterium-deuterium neutrons in a single shot, with an average yield around 5×10^11 neutrons per shot at 10 Torr deuterium. The company says this is the first publicly documented neutron yield at that level by any fusion company, delivering about 40% more neutrons per megajoule than Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory's MJOLNIR pulsed-power facility. FAETON-X reached the milestone nine months after its first shot. CEO JC Btaiche said 'fusion has reached an inflection point, and private companies are now at the forefront of technology development.' Fuse, based in San Leandro, California, generates near-term revenue from radiation-effects testing for defense and space customers while advancing toward commercial fusion energy.
confidenceReason: Based on company-reported results and a preprint (not yet peer-reviewed); independent verification of the neutron yield figures is pending.
